answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each new identity lock a refundable stake, then sending it through random cross-agent challenge rounds. A hidden committee compares signed claims and transaction histories across a dune market, a mirror service, and a grove of peers; inconsistent identities lose their stake and reputation. Thousands of fakes therefore demand capital for every account and expose the attacker to repeated slashing, so fabricating influence costs more than the payoff.
